info.title: D-API - Complete WhatsApp Infrastructure
info.description: A scalable, robust solution for automation managers, SaaS products and end users who need a reliable WhatsApp integration. It offers multiple simultaneous instances, real-time webhooks, an intuitive dashboard and a documented REST API with 99.9% uptime and latency under 30ms.

post.description: Sends a plain text message via WhatsApp

contextInfo.description: Whatsmeow ContextInfo proto JSON. Supports mentions, replies (quotedMessage), forwarding, ads, and other metadata.

participant.description: JID of who SENT the quoted message.

remoteJid.description: JID of the chat of the quoted message.

quotedMessage.description: Content of the quoted message (proto JSON), e.g. { conversation: "..." }.

sequential.description: With `async: true`, sends to THIS recipient go out one at a time, in the order the API received them. Sends to other recipients still run in parallel. This order is the order of arrival at the backend: requests fired in parallel by the client have no order to preserve — send them serially. There is a limit on accumulated pending sends per recipient; when it is exceeded the API responds 429 and the client should retry later. Ignored without `async: true` and in Official API sessions (`cloud_api`), where sending is always synchronous.

Sends an approved template through a Cloud API connection. Accepts body variables, a header variable/media (url or base64) and button parameters in `buttons[]` — the backend builds the Graph API components.

`buttons[]` is a union by `subType`: `url` (`text` — the suffix that replaces the {{1}} in the url), `copy_code` (`couponCode`), `flow` (`flowToken`, `flowActionData`), `order_details` and `payment_request` (`orderDetails`, with the amount in BRL). `index` is the button's position in the template, starting at 0. Quick reply does not accept parameters. `components` still exists as a raw escape hatch, but cannot be combined with `buttons`.

post.summary: Sync history (bulk) via webhook in D-API format
post.description: Bulk re-sends the instance's stored history to the webhook (D-API messages.received format). Default webhook: the one configured on the session (per_event uses the message received event's webhook); can be overridden with `webhookUrl` (required if the instance has no webhook). Includes media when the message has a media_url.

get.description: Returns the progress of the instance's latest history sync job (D-API format).

Gets the state and result of a command sent with `async: true`, by the `commandId` returned when enqueued.

`status`: `queued` (in the queue), `processing` (running), `completed` (executed — check `result.success` to know whether the command succeeded) or `failed` (the worker failed; see `error`).

The result is available for a limited queue retention window; for guaranteed delivery use the `command.result` webhook.

404.description: Command does not exist, expired from the queue or is outside the credential's scope

post.description: Lists business catalog products via the catalog_list command on the bridge.
Lists catalog collections via the catalog_collections_list command.
Gets a single catalog product via catalog_product_get.

Creates a product in the business catalog. price/sale_price are decimals (199.90 = R$ 199,90); the backend converts them to units × 1000 before sending to the bridge. is_hidden hides the product from the storefront (default false).
Edits fields of an existing product (patch — omitted fields keep their current value). price/sale_price are decimals; send sale_price=0 to remove the sale. is_hidden toggles visibility.
Removes a product from the catalog via catalog_product_delete.
Creates a catalog collection via catalog_collection_create. product_ids optionally pre-populates the collection.
Edits a collection. When product_ids is sent, it fully replaces the collection's members (it does not append).
Removes a collection from the catalog via catalog_collection_delete. The products themselves are not removed.
Triggers a FULL_HISTORY_SYNC_ON_DEMAND via PodWorker
Triggers a HISTORY_SYNC_ON_DEMAND via PodWorker; the 'count' query parameter sets how many messages to fetch (default 50)

get.description: Lists persisted live (stream) calls with their recording metadata, from newest to oldest. Restricted to the API Key owner's data. Supports pagination (page, limit — maximum 100) and the optional filters sessionId, phone and recordingStatus (uploaded | empty | failed).
Returns a persisted call (recording and transcription metadata, when available) by the dapi-go call_id. Restricted to the API Key owner's data.

post.description: Creates a new WhatsApp call link that can be shared for audio or video calls.
Sends a scheduled call or event message to a recipient. Can create a WhatsApp call link or use your own URL (Zoom, Meet, etc.).
Places an outgoing 1:1 voice call. Responds immediately with the callId (state "calling"); ringing, answer and hangup arrive as call.* webhook events.

Places an outgoing 1:1 call in live stream mode and returns a media WebSocket (wsUrl + token). Connect to the WS to stream microphone audio, hear the other side and receive the call lifecycle events. Every call is always recorded: a stereo WAV (microphone/remote party) is uploaded at the end of the call and the URL arrives as a final {type:'recording'} event on the WS. The legacy record field is accepted but ignored.

Answers an incoming WhatsApp call in live stream mode and returns a media WebSocket (wsUrl + token), in the same format as POST /calls/stream. Connect to the WS to stream microphone audio, hear the caller and receive the call lifecycle events. Use the `callId` from the call.offer event while the call is still ringing. Unavailable on cloud_api (Official API) connections.

post.summary: Create message template on the WABA
post.description:
Submits a new message template for Meta review. `name` must be lowercase snake_case; `category` is MARKETING, UTILITY or AUTHENTICATION; `language` is a Meta language code (e.g. pt_BR). Body placeholders use {{1}}, {{2}}… and `bodyExample` provides a sample value for each placeholder.

Headers: set `headerFormat` to TEXT (with `headerText`) or IMAGE/VIDEO/DOCUMENT (with `headerMediaUrl` or `headerMediaBase64` — the sample is sent to Meta automatically). Buttons: use `buttons[]` with QUICK_REPLY (`text`), URL (`text`, `url` — include `urlExample` when the url has {{1}}), PHONE_NUMBER (`text`, `phoneNumber`), COPY_CODE (`example`), FLOW (`text`, `flowId`, `flowAction` NAVIGATE/DATA_EXCHANGE, `navigateScreen`, `icon`) or PAYMENT_REQUEST (`text`, `paymentSetting.pixDynamicCode.code` — the Pix code lives in the template definition). `data` contains the created template's id and initial status (usually PENDING).

get.description: Lists ALL message templates of the connection's WABA, regardless of review status (APPROVED, PENDING, REJECTED, etc.) — use it in management screens. `data` is an array of Meta templates, including each one's `status`.

delete.description: Deletes a message template from the connection's WABA by name — this removes ALL language variants of that template. Returns `{ success: true }` when done.

get.summary: Get the decrypted Meta access token
get.description:
Returns the Meta access token stored for a cloud_api connection, DECRYPTED, along with the token type. The `id` accepts the connection id or the session id (`cloud-<uuid>`).

`data.accessToken` is the raw Graph token — treat it as a secret (it sends messages and manages the WABA). `data.kind` is `permanent` (never expires, e.g. System User), `long_lived` (~60-day token from Embedded Signup), `short_lived` (~1h token from the code exchange) or `unknown` (Meta's /debug_token could not be queried). `data.expiresAt` (ISO-8601, null when permanent), `data.expiresInDays`, `data.isValid`, `data.scopes`, `data.type` (Meta's own USER/SYSTEM_USER label) and `data.label` (summary in pt-BR) describe the token. To rotate it, use PATCH /connections/cloud-api/:id.

post.description: Creates a WhatsApp Official API connection from a waba id, phone number id and access token provided manually (generated in Meta Business Manager). Validates the (number, token) pair against the Graph API, tries to subscribe the app to webhooks and then provisions the connection and syncs Scale billing. `data` is `{ session, webhookSubscribed }` — show the manual subscription instructions when `webhookSubscribed` is false. Returns 402 (code TRIAL_REQUIRED) when the user has no active subscription.

Reports a contact to WhatsApp and, optionally, blocks it (report_contact). Response in data: { report: { status, report_id?, error? }, block?: { status, blocklist?, error? } }. success=true in the envelope means the bridge handled the request — not that both sub-steps succeeded. report.status='ok' with an empty report_id is a legitimate server-side discard (synthetic evidence) and is not an error. block is evaluated independently of report: it can fail (LID resolution miss) even when report is ok. Errors that fail the envelope (success=false): session not connected, invalid JID, empty recipient, warmup/rate-limit.
